title: Minimum wage Queensland: How it compares to the national minimum wage and state averages
description: Learn about the minimum wage in Queensland and how it compares to the national minimum wage. Use our hourly to annual conversion to estimate your pay, tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage in Queensland?
faqs.a: The minimum wage in Queensland is the National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1004.90 per week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week and then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, use: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44 per year.

faqs.q: How is tax calculated on my annual salary?
faqs.a: Tax uses the 2026–27 resident rates: nil up to $18,200, 15% to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. A 2% Medicare levy generally applies. The estimate assumes the full tax-free threshold and uses 2025–26 Medicare reduction thresholds.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the minimum wage queensland

If you are looking at the minimum wage queensland, it is important to know that the national minimum wage applies across Australia, including Queensland. From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. For casual employees, the rate includes a 25% casual loading, making it $33.05 per hour. However, many employees in Queensland are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that set higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides guidance on which award applies to your job.

### How the hourly to annual conversion works

To estimate your annual gross pay, multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week and then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, if you earn the national minimum wage of $26.44 per hour, your annual gross pay would be $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44 (approximately). This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to calculate your own figures.

### Fortnightly pay

If you are paid fortnightly, your gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For the national minimum wage, that would be $1004.90 × 2 = $2009.80 per fortnight before tax. This can help you budget if you are paid on a fortnightly cycle.

### Tax and superannuation

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates. The tax-free threshold is $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. A Medicare levy of 2% generally applies. For the minimum wage example of $52,269.44, the tax would be approximately: $0 on first $18,200, then 15% on $26,800 ($4,020), plus 2% Medicare ($1,045.39) = total tax and Medicare about $5,065.39. Your take-home pay would be around $47,204.05 per year. Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For the minimum wage example, your super would be about $6,272 per year. See our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for more details.

### How does Queensland compare?

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, the average full-time adult ordinary time earnings in Queensland for May 2026 were $2039.70 per week. This is an average across all industries and occupations, not the median for a specific job. It is significantly higher than the national minimum wage. The national average for all states was $2083.70 per week, so Queensland is slightly below the national average. If you are earning the minimum wage queensland, you may be below the state average. Use our [reference tables](/data) to compare different pay points.

### Minimum wage vs award rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Many workers in Queensland are covered by modern awards, which often have higher minimum rates. For example, the Hospitality Industry General Award or the Retail Award set higher rates for specific classifications. Casual employees also receive the 25% loading on top of the award rate. Check your award or agreement to ensure you are being paid correctly. You can find more information on our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page and [pay guides](/blog).

### Casual loading

If you are a casual employee, your hourly rate should include a 25% casual loading. This is in lieu of paid leave entitlements such as annual leave and sick leave. When using our [timesheet](/) tool, you can check the box to add 25% casual loading on top of your base rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading. For example, if your base rate is $26.44, the casual rate is $33.05. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains more.

### Superannuation is paid on top

Remember that superannuation is not deducted from your pay; it is paid on top by your employer. For the minimum wage example, your total employment cost to the employer is your gross pay plus 12% super. This is important when comparing salary offers or negotiating pay. The super guarantee rate is 12% from 1 July 2026, and it applies to ordinary earnings up to the maximum contribution base. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

### Using the timesheet

Our [timesheet](/) allows you to enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. The tool then calculates your annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay, as well as estimated tax and super. It assumes a 38-hour week, but you can adjust the hours if needed. The results are estimates and should not be relied upon for legal or financial decisions.

### Tax estimates disclaimer

The tax estimate uses the 2026–27 resident tax scale and the full tax-free threshold. Medicare levy is 2% based on the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. This is an estimate only. For a precise tax calculation, consult the Australian Taxation Office or a tax professional. The [about the timesheet](/about) page has full details.

### Conclusion

Whether you are on the minimum wage queensland or earning above it, understanding how your hourly rate translates to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay helps you budget and compare job offers. Use our tools and reference tables to get a clear picture of your earnings and obligations. Remember that the minimum wage in Queensland is the national minimum wage, but many workers earn more under awards or agreements. Always check your pay against the correct award.
